If the model above represents $1$ whole, use the model to solve the following division problem. Express your answer as a mixed number in its simplest form.

$1÷\frac{3}{8}=$
{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
To calculate $1÷\frac{3}{8}$, we first need to divide the whole into $8$ equal parts.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/e5c3ad39f7ebf8bb6585dfa65054bb6b0eba881f1e9f7404ae5275f5c45f3771.png)

 

Next, we break this into groups of $3$:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14144806/assets/dbfd34916dd6db9467988b6b72052f9b077e4de67e2b54b9a092d959233ccc85.png)

 

Note the following: 

- We got $\boxed{\text{2}}$ full groups.

- There are $2$ parts left over out of a possible group of $3.$ So the fractional part of our answer is 

$$
\frac{2}{3}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
1÷\frac{3}{8}=\boxed{\text{2}}\,\frac{2}{3}.
$$
